evidence.reference_title: Achromatopsia.
evidence.snippet: Achromatopsia is characterized by reduced visual acuity, pendular nystagmus, increased sensitivity to light (photophobia), a small central scotoma, eccentric fixation, and reduced or complete loss of color discrimination.

evidence.reference_title: Deep Phenotyping of PDE6C-Associated Achromatopsia.
evidence.snippet: All subjects presented with early-onset nystagmus, decreased best-corrected visual acuity, light sensitivity, and severe color vision loss, and five of them had high myopia.

evidence.reference_title: PDE6C / PDE6C-related retinopathy (Definitive)
evidence.snippet: Phenotypes generally occur with congenital or early childhood onset and include severe color vision defects, progressive loss of visual acuity over the course of decades, reduced or absent cone/photopic ERG responses, normal rod/scotopic ERG responses, photophobia, myopia, and/or nystagmus.

nodes.description: Without PDE6C-mediated hydrolysis, cone outer-segment cGMP stays elevated and the cyclic nucleotide-gated channels stay open, sustaining depolarising Na+/Ca2+ influx. The outer segment loses the cGMP and Ca2+ set point that the light response normally modulates.
nodes.id: Elevated Cone cGMP and Calcium Overload

nodes.description: With the cascade unable to lower cGMP, the cone cannot translate absorbed photons into the graded hyperpolarisation that signals light. Cone-driven (photopic) light responses are reduced or abolished while rod-driven (scotopic) responses are preserved, the electrophysiological signature of a cone-autonomous cascade defect.

evidence.reference_title: Homozygosity mapping reveals PDE6C mutations in patients with early-onset cone photoreceptor disorders.
evidence.snippet: Our findings identify PDE6C as a gene for cone photoreceptor disorders and show that arCD and ACHM constitute genetically and clinically overlapping phenotypes.

nodes.description: Biallelic PDE6C variants abolish or reduce the catalytic activity of the cone-specific alpha-prime subunit of cGMP phosphodiesterase 6. PDE6 is the effector that hydrolyses cGMP to 5'-GMP during the cone light response, so a catalytic-subunit lesion is the initiating, cone-autonomous defect in the phototransduction cascade.

evidence.reference_title: Homozygosity mapping reveals PDE6C mutations in patients with early-onset cone photoreceptor disorders.
evidence.snippet: The PDE6C gene encodes the cone alpha subunit of cyclic guanosine monophosphate (cGMP) phosphodiesterase, which converts cGMP to 5'-GMP, and thereby plays an essential role in cone phototransduction.

nodes.description: In the degenerative pole of the spectrum, chronically elevated cGMP and Ca2+ drive progressive death of cone photoreceptors, with thinning of the outer nuclear layer and loss of outer-segment structure most marked in the macula. This is the cone-dystrophy (cone dystrophy 4) end of the PDE6C spectrum, and is more pronounced in complete achromatopsia than in early-onset cone dystrophy.
